title: Signals
description:
The **observer** pattern lets one object announce that something happened without knowing who is listening. A button does not call the save code; it emits "clicked", and whoever connected to that gets called.

In modern C++ the listeners are simply callables. Write `template <typename... Args> class Signal`:

- `int connect(std::function<void(Args...)> listener)`: adds a listener and returns an id for it. Ids are never reused.
- `bool disconnect(int id)`: removes that listener; returns whether it was found.
- `void emit(Args... args) const`: calls every connected listener, in the order they connected.
- `std::size_t listenerCount() const`

One detail makes the difference between a toy and something usable: a listener may disconnect itself (or another listener) **while `emit` is running**. Looping directly over the container while it changes underneath you is undefined behaviour. The simplest safe approach is to loop over a copy.
